items.title: The actual matrix-Chebyshev cosine identity

source.anchor: Eq11; S4.SS3.p3.1,p3.2,p4.1 intrinsic first-kind polynomial detector and cosine coordinate bridge
source.attribution: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling, arXiv2610.20492v1.
source.scope: Explicit auxiliary matrix identity/generalization and private literal pushforward-event component, not full Theorem4.1 or Ex26.

items.statement: The first-kind Chebyshev polynomial of the normalized hard-family precision is its same-rotation cosine diagonal. T_n\!\left(\frac{2A-(\kappa+1)I_d}{\kappa-1}\right)=O\,\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(\cos(n\theta_i)\bigr)O^\top. Let \(d\ge2\) be natural, \(\kappa\ge2\) real, and \(O\in O(d)\) a full real orthogonal matrix. Both determinant signs are allowed. This is a fixed-input algebraic statement, with no algorithm or Haar-independence premise. Use the literal midpoint grid \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), precision eigenvalues \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)\), and \(A=O\Lambda O^\top\). Lean's zero-based coordinate is \(i_{\rm val}+\tfrac12\). The auxiliary identity holds for every natural \(n\), including zero. The source proof specializes to \(n=2q+1\). \(T_n\) is the usual first-kind polynomial; its matrix evaluation maps real coefficients to scalar identity matrices. The private application allows every real \(\tau\), with source instance \(\tau_{d,q}\). Put \(\mu=N(0,\Lambda^{-1})\), \(Rz=Oz\), \(S_A(x)=(-1)^n x^\top T_n((2A-(\kappa+1)I_d)/(\kappa-1))x-2\tau\|x\|^2\), and \(E_A=\{S_A>0\}\). It proves Borelness and a literal \(\mu\circ R^{-1}\) event-mass equality; identifying that law with \(\pi_A\) remains separate. Scalar \((\kappa-1)^{-1}\) in the normalized matrix and matrix \(\Lambda^{-1}\) in the Gaussian covariance are different operations. Nonzero scalar domain, orthogonal identities, continuity and measurability are produced internally. No moment, probability, rotation-law, query-budget or cost certificate is an input.
